proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu served as Chancellor, Yu Chi raised a rebellion at Xiangzhou. Shu, acting as campaign commander-in-chief, led three thousand foot and horse soldiers to join Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu served as Chancellor, Yuchi Jiong raised a rebellion at Xiangzhou. Shu, acting as campaign commander-in-chief, led three thousand foot and horse soldiers to join Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉迥 abbreviates 尉遲迥; English wrongly splits the surname as 'Yu Chi' instead of Yuchi Jiong.

proposals.before: He also joined the other generals in attacking Yu Dun at Yong Bridge. Shu led the vanguard through the enemy formation and took a great many prisoners and heads.
proposals.after: He also joined the other generals in attacking Yuchi Dun at Yong Bridge. Shu led the vanguard through the enemy formation and took a great many prisoners and heads.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉惇 is Yuchi Dun; 'Yu Dun' mis-splits the compound surname 尉遲.

proposals.before: In the campaign to put down Yu Chi, he distinguished himself in every battle. He was promoted out of turn to Superior Pillar of State, raised to Duke of Bao, and granted three thousand bolts of silk.
proposals.after: In the campaign to put down Yuchi Jiong, he distinguished himself in every battle. He was promoted out of turn to Superior Pillar of State, raised to Duke of Bao, and granted three thousand bolts of silk.
proposals.reason: Same surname error as s0009: 尉迥 is Yuchi Jiong, not Yu Chi.

proposals.before: Mundeok again sent envoys in feigned surrender, telling Shu, "If you withdraw your army, we will present King Goguryeo at his traveling palace."
proposals.after: Mundeok again sent envoys in feigned surrender, telling Shu, "If you withdraw your army, we will present Gao Yuan at his traveling palace."
proposals.reason: Chinese 高元 is the personal name Gao Yuan, not the title 'King Goguryeo'.

proposals.before: Mundeok again sent envoys in feigned surrender, requesting of Shu, "If you withdraw your army, we will present King Goguryeo at his traveling palace."
proposals.after: Mundeok again sent envoys in feigned surrender, requesting of Shu, "If you withdraw your army, we will present Gao Yuan at his traveling palace."
proposals.reason: Literal likewise invents 'King Goguryeo' for 高元.

proposals.before: Soon he replaced He Chou as Assistant Supervisor, was transferred to Junior Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was promoted to Left Imperial Guard General, and still oversaw the affairs of the Palace Storehouse.
proposals.after: Soon he replaced He Chou as Assistant Supervisor, was transferred to Junior Director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia, was promoted to Left Imperial Guard General, and still oversaw the affairs of the Palace Storehouse.
proposals.reason: 衛尉少卿 is Junior Director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia/Guards, not the Imperial Stud (太僕).

proposals.before: Soon he replaced He Chou as Assistant Supervisor, was transferred to Junior Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was promoted to Left Imperial Guard General, and still oversaw the affairs of the Palace Storehouse.
proposals.after: Soon he replaced He Chou as Assistant Supervisor, was transferred to Junior Director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia, was promoted to Left Imperial Guard General, and still oversaw the affairs of the Palace Storehouse.
proposals.reason: Same 衛尉/太僕 office mistranslation in the literal field.

proposals.before: The emperor issued an edict from above and below saying, "Sir, your great merit and vast achievement, your lofty name and heavy prestige, and your long-known loyalty to the state are well understood.
proposals.after: The emperor issued an edict saying, "Sir, your great merit and vast achievement, your lofty name and heavy prestige, and your long-known loyalty to the state are well understood.
proposals.reason: Chinese 上下詔曰 is corrupt/awkward for 上詔曰; 'from above and below' is a nonsense calque.

proposals.before: Shu advanced, broke through the palisades, turned his army to strike Kan, and inflicted a crushing defeat, beheading Kan's marshal of the left, Cao Lecha.
proposals.after: Shu advanced, broke through the palisades, turned his army to strike Kan, and inflicted a crushing defeat, beheading Kan's marshal Cao Lecha.
proposals.reason: 司馬 means marshal/sima; 'of the left' is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: When Yu Chi raised a rebellion, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in battle at Wuzhi and advanced to fight at Xiangzhou.
proposals.after: When Yuchi Jiong raised a rebellion, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in battle at Wuzhi and advanced to fight at Xiangzhou.
proposals.reason: 尉迥 is Yuchi Jiong throughout.

proposals.before: He again followed in the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Jingshan route and receiving more than twenty thousand households of the Jiang people.
proposals.after: He again followed in the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Jinshan route and receiving more than twenty thousand households of the Jiang people.
proposals.reason: Chinese 金山 is Jinshan (“Golden Mountain”), not Jingshan; the route name was mistranslated.

proposals.before: He again followed in the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Jingshan route and receiving more than twenty thousand households of the Jiang.
proposals.after: He again followed in the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Jinshan route and receiving more than twenty thousand households of the Jiang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 金山 is Jinshan, not Jingshan; the literal English repeats the same error.

proposals.before: When the emperor died, Prince Han of Han raised a rebellion while the capital was empty; Yan was sent to ride back in haste and take overall command to hold the defense.
proposals.after: When the emperor died, the Prince of Han raised a rebellion while the capital was empty; Yan was sent to ride back in haste and take overall command to hold the defense.
proposals.reason: 漢王 is Prince of Han; “Prince Han of Han” doubles the polity name unnaturally.

decisions.reason: s0009 尉迥 abbreviates 尉遲迥 (Yuchi Jiong); 'Yu Chi' wrongly splits the compound Xianbei surname 尉遲, and the proposed idiomatic restores the historical name without other changes.
s0011 尉惇 is likewise the Yuchi surname plus given name Dun; 'Yu Dun' mis-splits 尉遲, and 'Yuchi Dun' matches the Chinese.
s0012 平尉迥 again names Yuchi Jiong; replacing 'Yu Chi' with 'Yuchi Jiong' corrects the same surname split without altering the rest of the sentence.
s0088 奉高元朝行在所 uses the personal name 高元; 'King Goguryeo' invents a title the Chinese does not write, and 'Gao Yuan' is the accurate rendering.
The literal field of s0088 likewise invents 'King Goguryeo' for 高元; the proposed replacement restores the personal name in the quoted pledge.
s0139 衛尉少卿 is the junior directorate of the Court of Imperial Insignia (衛尉), not the Court of the Imperial Stud (太僕); the proposed office title corrects that mistranslation.
The literal of s0139 repeats the same 衛尉/太僕 error; 'Court of the Imperial Insignia' matches 衛尉少卿.

Wikisource Suishu juan 61 transmits the same 上下詔曰, so the Chinese is not a unique local corruption, but 'from above and below' is still a nonsense calque of 上下; dropping it yields natural English for an imperial edict, matching the idiomatic.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上下詔曰：「公鴻勳大業，名高望重，奉國之誠，久所知悉。

decisions.reason: s0027 斬瓛司馬曹勒叉 names only 司馬 (marshal); 'of the left' invents 左, and removing it restores the Chinese office title.
s0158 尉迥之起逆 is again Yuchi Jiong; 'Yu Chi' is the same erroneous surname split, and the proposed idiomatic corrects it.
s0202 出金山道 is the Jinshan route; 'Jingshan' misreads 金 as 京/Jing and invents a different place name.
The literal of s0202 repeats Jingshan for 金山道; Jinshan is the correct reading of 金山.
s0199 漢王 is the Prince of Han; 'Prince Han of Han' doubles the fief name, and 'the Prince of Han' is the accurate title rendering.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 (and supporting r0003/r0010) shows English 'Yu Chi' came only from mis-splitting 尉迥; the personal-name claim must read Yuchi Jiong while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0002 shows English 'Yu Dun' came only from mis-splitting 尉惇; the personal-name claim must read Yuchi Dun while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
